Each region is therefore cross-checked against the neutral same-cloud control hostname ec2.<region>.amazonaws.com (full HTTP 301, TLS and TTFB available); the two TCP medians agree within about 1-5 ms, which is what licenses the proxy-host timing to be read as true cloud-region RTT rather than a same-named CDN.

reasoning: The only latency-critical database caller is server-side and it is fixed: the authoritative Game Core A/B and the initial durable worker run on the Oracle host in region iad / US-ASHBURN-AD-1 (docs/v5/ARCHITECTURE.md lines 10-19, spec 04 line 28 'region near IAD'), and the stateless API runs on Vercel. Measured Core-to-region RTT is 3.3 ms for aws-us-east-1 versus 14.8 ms (Ohio), 75-90 ms (EU), 116 ms (Sao Paulo), 200-236 ms (APAC). Serialized-lock command transactions pay that RTT several times per commit, so the APAC options are unusable for the hot path.

Clients never connect to PostgreSQL (browser/native clients reach the Vercel API and the Oracle Core over one-use ticket + revision resume), so owner/player geography cannot be served by moving the database region. The owner workstation in Bengaluru measures 47-49 ms to aws-ap-southeast-1 versus 216-301 ms to the staging hostnames, but that difference lands on human console/diagnostic traffic only, not on gameplay; the existing V4 edge already costs 707-870 ms total TLS GET from the same workstation, dwarfing any DB choice.

aws-us-east-1 is also the catalogued default (default true) and is one of the four regions where the provider enables its newer products, which keeps later options open. It is the same AWS metro as the Oracle authority site (verified by matching neutral ec2.us-east-1.amazonaws.com timings), so no cross-region hop is introduced.

Azure candidates were rejected on evidence, not assumption: GET /regions still advertises azure-eastus2, azure-westus3 and azure-gwc, provider documentation states new project creation there has been blocked since 2026-04-07, and the guessed Azure proxy hostnames do not even resolve. Neon also fixes region at project creation with no in-place change, so a wrong choice is an expensive mistake.
region_decision.latency_versus_jurisdiction_tradeoff: V4's only APAC anchor is the Cloudflare R2 backup bucket mega-xo-backups created with APAC/default placement (docs/V4-OPEN-BLOCKERS.md EXT-07). That is a backup-copy placement decision on Cloudflare's side, not a residency rule on the live store: per Cloudflare's own data-location reference, enforceable jurisdictions are only eu, fedramp and us, while apac/oc are best-effort location hints and automatic placement follows the requester. Meanwhile the V4 authority - the SQLite database and every player row - already resides on the Oracle host in US Ashburn (region iad), and V5's own R2 recovery repository is an independently chosen destination (spec 04 backups section, gate P15). Choosing aws-us-east-1 therefore adds no new jurisdiction exposure relative to the existing authority, and holding the staging project in APAC would buy zero latency benefit for players while inserting about 236 ms into every Core-to-PostgreSQL transaction. If a future legal review (EXT-21, jurisdictions still unresolved) imposes genuine data-residency duties on durable truth, that decision must move the Core and the database together and cannot be solved by the Neon region alone.
region_decision.provisionality: The staging region is now measured and consistent with the parent's provisioning, so it is no longer provisional for staging. The production project region is NOT decided by this evidence: always-on and a restore window beyond 6 hours are not reachable on Free (G04/G05), and a production region must be chosen only after those plan decisions are recorded.

review_notes: Read-only throughout: only GET requests plus provider CLI read commands and network probes were issued; the two write-capable commands that were exercised are the documented negative probes (placeholder/nonexistent ids) which the API rejected. No credential reveal endpoint (reveal_password, connection_uri) was called and no token value is reproduced; captured token ids and personal fields were redacted in the private directory. Nothing was created, suspended, restored, resized or deleted, and the Oracle host was touched only by read commands (IMDS metadata, curl timings, a python one-liner over stdin) with no file written outside an immediately deleted transient copy and no access to /opt/mega-xo, no container and no service change. One probe attempt against the Oracle host initially failed with 'node: command not found' and is preserved as a recorded failure with the python fallback result; three HTTPS probes to guessed Azure proxy hostnames returned could-not-resolve and are preserved as failures rather than retried further.
